options: Temporary Reference Number, generated during registration after Part A
exp: TRN: Temporary Reference Number, generated during registration after Part A.

q: What does ARN stand for in GST?
options: Application Reference Number, given on submitting an application or return
exp: ARN: Application Reference Number, given on submitting an application or return.

q: What does CPIN stand for in GST?
options: Common Portal Identification Number, generated for a challan
exp: CPIN: Common Portal Identification Number, generated for a challan.

q: What does CIN (in GST payments) stand for in GST?
options: Challan Identification Number, generated by the bank after payment
exp: CIN (in GST payments): Challan Identification Number, generated by the bank after payment.

q: What does LUT stand for in GST?
options: Letter of Undertaking, to export without paying IGST
exp: LUT: Letter of Undertaking, to export without paying IGST.

options: Unique Identity Number given to embassies, UN bodies and similar organisations
exp: UIN: Unique Identity Number given to embassies, UN bodies and similar organisations.

exp: OIDAR: Online Information Database Access and Retrieval services.

q: What does AATO stand for in GST?

q: What does ISD stand for in GST?

q: What does CDNR stand for in GST?

options: Business to Consumer Large: inter-state invoices to unregistered buyers above the value limit

q: Under GST, 'business' includes:
options: Any trade, commerce, manufacture, profession or similar activity, whether or not for profit, and even activities incidental to it
exp: The definition is deliberately wide.

q: A 'casual taxable person' is someone who:
options: Occasionally supplies goods or services in a state where they have no fixed place of business
exp: E.g. exhibitors at a trade fair in another state.

q: 'Related persons' under GST include:
options: Officers or directors of each other's businesses, employer and employee, partners, persons controlling each other, and specified family members
exp: Explanation to s.15 lists them. It matters for valuation and Schedule I.

q: A 'distinct person' under GST refers to:
options: Registrations of the same PAN in different states, or separate verticals in one state
exp: Supplies between distinct persons are taxable even without consideration.

q: An 'intermediary' under IGST law is:
options: A broker or agent who arranges or facilitates supplies between two or more persons, but not someone who supplies on their own account
exp: The distinction decides place of supply for many Indian firms serving foreign clients.

q: 'Input' under GST means:
options: Any goods other than capital goods, used or intended to be used in the course of business
exp: 'Input service' covers services, and 'capital goods' are goods capitalised in the books.

q: 'Principal place of business' is:
options: The place specified as the principal place in the registration certificate
exp: It matters for bill-to ship-to place of supply and for notices.

q: 'Job work' means:
options: Undertaking any treatment or process on goods belonging to another registered person
exp: Principals can send goods to job workers under a delivery challan without paying tax, subject to return timelines.

q: Under section 143, inputs sent to a job worker must be brought back within:
options: 1 year (3 years for capital goods), extendable
exp: If not returned in time, it's deemed a supply on the date the goods were sent.

q: 'Reverse charge' is defined as:
options: Liability to pay tax by the recipient instead of the supplier
exp: Under sections 9(3), 9(4) and 5(3)/(4) of IGST.

q: Nil-rated vs exempt vs non-GST: which pair is correctly matched?
options: Nil-rated: rate is 0% in the tariff; exempt: notified as exempt by notification; non-GST: outside GST law entirely (like alcohol)
exp: All three are reported separately in GSTR-1 Table 8, and all block ITC for the related inputs.

q: GSTR-2A vs GSTR-2B:
options: 2A is dynamic (keeps updating); 2B is a static monthly snapshot used for ITC
exp: Neither is 'filed'. Both are auto-generated statements.

q: CGST vs IGST:
options: CGST is the Centre's share on intra-state supplies; IGST is levied on inter-state supplies and imports
exp: Intra-state: CGST + SGST/UTGST. Inter-state: IGST.

q: Credit note vs debit note:
options: Credit note reduces the value or tax charged; debit note increases it
exp: Both are issued by the supplier under section 34.

q: 'Bill of supply' vs 'bill of entry':
options: A bill of supply is issued for exempt supplies or by composition taxpayers; a bill of entry is the customs document for imports
Bill of entry is for exports
exp: The bill of entry is filed on ICEGATE and the IGST paid on it becomes ITC.

q: 'Zero-rated' vs 'exempt':
options: Zero-rated keeps ITC (refundable); exempt loses ITC on related inputs
exp: This is one of the most tested distinctions.

q: 'Composite supply' vs 'mixed supply':
options: Composite: naturally bundled, taxed at principal supply's rate; mixed: not naturally bundled, taxed at the highest rate
exp: Section 8.

q: 'Aggregate turnover' vs 'turnover in state':
options: Aggregate turnover is PAN-level all-India; turnover in state is for a single state's registration
exp: Registration threshold and e-invoice use aggregate turnover; composition tax is computed on turnover in state.
